title: Localization at a face and sharpening of an fs monoid
statement: Let $Q$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively. Let $F\subseteq Q$ be a face: $F$ is a submonoid and $a+b\in F$ implies $a,b\in F$. Inside the group completion $Q^{\rm gp}$ put $Q_F=\{q-f:q\in Q,\ f\in F\}$, and let $F^{\rm gp}$ be the subgroup generated by $F$. Then $Q_F$ is fine saturated and its group of units is exactly $F^{\rm gp}$. The quotient $R=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$, where elements differing by an element of $F^{\rm gp}$ are identified, is a fine saturated sharp monoid (sharp means that $0$ is its only invertible element), and the canonical map $R\to Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ is injective and identifies the latter group with $R^{\rm gp}$. Moreover $R^{\rm gp}$ is a free abelian group of finite rank, meaning it has a finite basis over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 98--99 (localization and sharpening); Expose VI, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 70 and 75 (the sharp fs characteristic and its finitely generated torsion-free group). Algebraic input to the sharp-chart step in the monoidal-resolution ancestry of lem-trf-local-term-locality, proof (1)--(2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-face-localization-fs] to the given fine saturated monoid Q and its face F. The set Q_F in the statement is the localization at F, so it is fine saturated and its group completion is canonically Q^{\rm gp}.

By [lem-trf-face-localization-units], the units of Q_F are exactly F^{\rm gp}. Thus the quotient R=Q_F/F^{\rm gp} is sharp: if a class is invertible, a representative is a unit modulo the subgroup of units, so the class is the zero class.

The quotient of a finitely generated monoid by its subgroup of units is finitely generated. Integrality is inherited because the quotient is formed inside the group quotient Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}; saturation is inherited from the saturation of Q_F after multiplying a class by a positive integer and lifting the resulting equality. Therefore R is fine saturated and sharp.

The canonical map R→Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp} is induced by the inclusion Q_F⊂Q^{\rm gp}. If two classes have the same image, their representatives differ by an element of F^{\rm gp}, hence by a unit of Q_F, so the classes in R are equal; the map is injective. Since Q_F^{\rm gp}≅Q^{\rm gp} by Step 1 and quotienting a commutative monoid by its units commutes with group completion, it identifies R^{\rm gp} with Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}.

By [lem-trf-face-subgroup-saturated], F^{\rm gp} is a saturated subgroup of Q^{\rm gp} (if $nx\in F^{\rm gp}$ with $n>0$ then $x\in F^{\rm gp}$); hence Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}, and therefore R^{\rm gp}, is torsion-free. The group is finitely generated because Q^{\rm gp} is generated by the finite generating set of Q and the quotient of a finitely generated group is finitely generated.

proof.text: Apply the Mathlib leaf [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to the finitely generated torsion-free abelian group R^{\rm gp}. It supplies a finite Z-basis, so R^{\rm gp} is free abelian of finite rank.

lean.statement: theorem face_sharpening (Q : Type u) [CommMonoid Q] (hQ : IsFineSaturatedMonoid Q) (F : Submonoid Q) (hF : ∀ a b : Q, a * b ∈ F → a ∈ F ∧ b ∈ F) : let R := Associates (Algebra.faceLocalization Q F) let H := Subgroup.closure (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of '' (F : Set Q)) IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Algebra.faceLocalization Q F) ∧ (∀ x : Algebra.faceLocalization Q F, IsUnit x ↔ (x : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup Q) ∈ H) ∧ IsFineSaturatedMonoid R ∧ (∀ r : R, IsUnit r → r = 1) ∧ ∃ φ : R →* (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup Q ⧸ H), (∀ x : Algebra.faceLocalization Q F, φ (Associates.mk x) = QuotientGroup.mk' H (Algebra.faceLocalizationGroupMap F (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of x))) ∧ Function.Injective φ ∧ (∃ e : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup R ≃* (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup Q ⧸ H), ∀ r : R, e (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of r) = φ r) ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ (Additive (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup R))))
